findings.title: Explicit `render :show` runs before `canonical_url` is set, breaking canonical links on topic pages
findings.body:
`perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` inside the `format.html` block, so the page and layout render immediately. In `show`, `canonical_url ...` is called afterwards (line 87). Previously the implicit render ran at the end of the action, after `@canonical_url` was set.

Now the layout's canonical link tag sees no `@canonical_url` and falls back to the default (the raw request URL). Every topic HTML page loses its proper `<link rel="canonical">`. For example, `/t/slug/123/45` becomes its own canonical instead of the topic's canonical path. This is an SEO regression affecting all topic views.

Fix: move the `canonical_url` call above `perform_show_response`, or render `:show` explicitly only in `unsubscribe`.

findings.title: NoMethodError when user has no TopicUser row for the topic
findings.body:
`TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` returns nil when the user has never had a topic_users record for this topic. A logged-in user can hit `/t/slug/:id/unsubscribe` for any visible topic, or a row may have been removed. The next line, `tu.notification_level > ...`, then raises NoMethodError and returns a 500.

Fix: handle the nil case, e.g. by using `TopicUser.change` to create or update the row.

findings.title: Saving TopicUser directly leaves notifications_reason_id nil, so auto-tracking silently undoes the unsubscribe
findings.body:
The action sets `notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, bypassing `TopicUser.change`. `change` would also set `notifications_reason_id = user_changed`, set `notifications_changed_at`, and publish the MessageBus `notification_level_change`.

Because the reason stays NULL, the SQL in `TopicUser.update_last_read` will overwrite the level with `tracking` the next time the user reads the topic past the auto-track threshold. That SQL runs `case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null and total_msecs_viewed > threshold then :tracking`. `auto_track` also only acts on rows with a nil reason. Users who were auto-tracked by reading, which is the common case, therefore get re-subscribed as soon as they open the topic again. Open browser tabs also never learn about the level change.

Fix: use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

findings.title: Non-idempotent state-changing GET; first click doesn't actually stop notifications
findings.body:
The unsubscribe link is a GET that toggles state. If the level is above regular it drops to regular; otherwise it mutes.

Two consequences:
1. Email link scanners and prefetchers (e.g. Outlook Safe Links, corporate gateways) or a second click will step the user further, from watching/tracking to regular and then to muted, without the user's intent.
2. A tracking or watching user who receives a reply/mention/quote email and clicks "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" is only set to `regular`. Regular still receives reply, mention and quote notifications and emails. Yet both the email text and the page ("You will stop receiving notifications for ...") claim notifications have stopped.

The action should set an explicit target level (e.g. muted) idempotently, or the copy should match the behavior.

findings.title: Unsubscribe link from email requires an active session
findings.body: `:unsubscribe` was added to `ensure_logged_in`. Users frequently click email links in a browser or client where they are not logged in. They will get the NotLoggedIn handling (redirect to `/` or a 403) and the unsubscribe never happens. The intended URL is not preserved for after login, so the user lands somewhere unrelated with no explanation. Consider storing the destination and redirecting to login.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link caller
findings.body:
The `unsubscribe_link` string in server.en.yml now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and it is rendered in both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true.

Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when building the email. Such callers include other mailers or plugins, and any non-topic email. The existing spec had to be modified to pass `unsubscribe_url` for exactly this reason.

Fix: make the per-topic sentence conditional (separate key appended only when `unsubscribe_url` is present), or default the argument.

findings.title: Overriding computed `details.notificationReasonText` leaks into the identity-mapped topic
findings.body:
`store.createRecord('topic', { id })` with an id hydrates through the store's identity map. The topic route later reuses the same Topic and TopicDetails instance when the user navigates to `/t/slug/id`.

Setting `details.notificationReasonText` to null overrides the computed property on that object. After visiting the unsubscribe page and then opening the topic in the same session, the notification reason text stays blank and no longer updates when the level changes.

Fix: hide the text in this template or view instead of mutating the shared model.

findings.title: In-app navigation to the unsubscribe URL shows confirmation without changing anything
findings.body:
The client route `topicUnsubscribe` only loads the topic via `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which hits `/t/:id.json`. It never calls the server `unsubscribe` action. The state change happens only on a full page load.

If the URL is followed inside the running Ember app, the page says "You will stop receiving notifications" but the notification level is untouched. Discourse intercepts same-origin links, so this happens with a link pasted in a post or reached through browser history.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe behavior
